text:
A low-carbohydrate intake reduces glycogen stores and carbohydrate availability, which can impair high-intensity exercise performance and cause fatigue. It may promote fat oxidation and aid weight loss for some, but can bring short-term side effects and, if sustained, risks inadequate fiber and micronutrient intake unless carefully planned. Overall, it can suit specific goals but requires monitoring for nutritional adequacy and individual tolerance.
